title: Schalke return to the Bundesliga: Karius, Dzeko and Muslic impress as German giants promoted
content:
Schalke have won promotion back to the top division of German football after a three-year absence following Saturday night’s 1-0 win over Fortuna Dusseldorf.

The victory, courtesy of a first-half goal from Kenan Karaman, put Miron Muslic’s side an unassailable 10 points clear of third-place Hannover, who have just three league matches remaining in 2.Bundesliga.

It also moves Schalke nine points ahead of second-place Paderborn, and needing just one point from their remaining three matches to clinch the second-tier title.

Schalke have been outscored by six league rivals this season, with as many goals scored (49) as 16th-place Magdeburg, but Muslic’s side’s success has been built on their league-best defence (28 goals conceded).

Saturday night’s victory was Schalke’s fifth in a row and their strong recent form has seen them defeated just once in their last 13 league games.

Schalke, who reached the Champions League semi-final stage in 2011 and won the UEFA Cup — the predecessor to the Europa League — are one of Germany’s biggest clubs, but, despite finishing runners-up on seven occasions, they have never won the Bundesliga.

The Gelsenkirchen-based club were crowned champions of Germany on seven times before the league’s formation in 1962, when there was a national cup format.

Promotion out of the 2.Bundesliga is no easy task, even for a club as large as Schalke. Famously, Hamburg spent seven years trying to return to the top flight following relegation, before finally emerging last season, and the division remains home to all sorts of fallen giants: Kaiserslautern, Nuremberg, Dusseldorf.

But Schalke have done it — this was their third attempt and despite never threatening promotion before, they have been by far and away the best and most consistent team in the division.

It’s a side full of stories. Loris Karius arrived as a back-up goalkeeper last season, but has produced some of the best form of his career to recover his reputation in Germany and become the undisputed number one. Edin Dzeko joined on a free transfer from Fiorentina in January and, even at 40, has managed a steady beat of goal involvements that have allowed Schalke to navigate what, traditionally, is always a chaotic time of year.

Those are the headline names, but Kenan Karaman might be the club’s player of the year. Now 32, the former Turkey international joined during the relegation season in 2022-23 and has been consistently outstanding. Even in those first two seasons, during which Schalke were mediocre even by second-division standards, Karaman was — as he has been again this season — excellent.

Adil Aouchiche and Soufian El-Faouzi, both 23, have emerged as excellent midfielders of complimentary profiles, who will surely only develop further next season at a higher level.

Lastly, what a triumph for coach Muslic. The 43-year-old left Plymouth Argyle under a cloud last summer, becoming the fifth different permanent Schalke coach since 2022, but the Bosnian has succeeded where many others have failed.

Schalke have been one of German football’s most confusing riddles. Over the past decade a half, they have laboured under the weight of off-field dysfunction and historic expectation — home games attract over 60,000 fans, even in the 2.Bundesliga — and have seemed like a question without an answer. It has been a very, very long way back.

They are not there yet. Eight years ago, they finished second in the Bundesliga and were playing in the Champions League. There are still many rungs to climb if Schalke are really to be Schalke again. Last time they were relegated, back in 2021, they returned after a single season, only to be immediately relegated back with barely a fight. So, there is caution to be taken and work to do if the they are to remain on an upward trend.

But this is a big moment and the club are significant enough that everyone, regardless of loyalty, will be glad to see them back where they belong.
